images.filename: Christening of USS Micka (DE-176) at Federal Shipbuilding and Drydock Company, New Jersey (USA), 23 August 1943 (NH 96611).jpg
images.caption:
Mrs. Evelyn Vandenberg Micka, widow of the late Lieutenant Edward Micka, USN, sponsor of the ship, holds her 10-month old daughter Barbara Lynn Micka, during launching ceremonies of the U.S. Navy destroyer escort USS Micka (DE-176) at the Federal Shipbuilding and Drydock Company, Newark, New Jersey (USA), 23 August 1943.
Lieutenant Micka was assigned to Fighting Squadron 9 (VF-9) aboard the aircraft carrier USS Ranger (CV-4). He was killed during an attack on the Mediouna airdrome, Morocco, during "Operation Torch", on 9 November 1942.
images.alt:
Mrs. Evelyn Vandenberg Micka, widow of the late Lieutenant Edward Micka, USN, sponsor of the ship, holds her 10-month old daughter Barbara Lynn Micka, during launching ceremonies of the U.S. Navy destroyer escort USS Micka (DE-176) at the Federal Shipbuilding and Drydock Company, Newark, New Jersey (USA), 23 August 1943.
Lieutenant Micka was assigned to Fighting Squadron 9 (VF-9) aboard the aircraft carrier USS Ranger (CV-4). He was killed during an attack on the Mediouna airdrome, Morocco, during "Operation Torch", on 9 November 1942.

images.filename: High point monument.jpg
images.caption:
The monument located in High Point State Park. 
The monument was built to honor war veterans, through the generosity of the Kusers. Construction began in 1928 and completed in 1930. At the top of the 220-foot structure, observers have a spectacular view of the ridges of the Pocono Mountains toward the west, the Catskill Mountains to the north and the Wallkill River Valley in the southeast. At the top of New Jersey's tallest knob, the Monument is an obelisk monument similar to other war monuments, such as the one located on Bunker Hill in Massachusetts.
images.alt:
